title: Chanee durian (Thai Chanee): Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaTitle: Chanee durian: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaDescription: Chanee durian is a durian variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best. Compare it with others.
excerpt: Chanee is a registered durian variety, also sold or known as Thai Chanee. The Philippine Seed Board approved it in 1991.

heroImage.alt: Young fruit trees planted in straight rows on cleared red soil, the kind of farm where Chanee durian is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Thai Chanee, this is the same durian. Its seller and farm sources add notes, listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [durian variety finder](/crop-varieties/durian), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for fruit trees](/land-preparation/fruit-tree-land-preparation).
When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

anee.io keeps the records of each block of trees, from fertilizer to harvest, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside them.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.
The pests and diseases that hit durian fields most often: [mealybug](/pests/mealybug). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
A fruit of Chanee weighs about 2000 grams, and its shape is conical. The flesh is smooth and fine. The edible part is 31.65 percent of the fruit.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Fruit:** Conical, about 2 kg, almond green, smooth, fine flesh, mild aroma, about 32 percent edible.
Registered in 1991 with the Philippine Seed Board.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: thai durian that is a parent of Arancillo and Puyat. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Chanee durian

Davao growers plant named clones such as Puyat and Arancillo for their thick, creamy flesh and small seeds. Plant grafted trees of a known clone, and mix clones for better fruit set. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Thai Chanee the same as Chanee?
items.a: Yes. Thai Chanee is another name for Chanee. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of Chanee?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
